items.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Bioengineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA.; Gladstone Institutes, San Francisco, CA, USA.; Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences, University of California San Francisco, San Francisco, CA, USA.
items.abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((k cat /K M )/k w ) of up to 3 x 10 13 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

items.title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Silicon and Advanced Semiconductor Materials and School of Materials Science and Engineering, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, P. R. China.; ZJU-Hangzhou Global Scientific and Technological Innovation Center, Hangzhou, P. R. China.
items.abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

items.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Environment and Sustainability, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong SAR, China.; Department of Chemistry, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong SAR, China.
items.abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year −1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year −1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year −1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

items.title: The scientific record is never finished
items.last_author_affiliation: Valda Vinson is the Executive Editor of the Science journals.
items.abstract: The scholarly scientific record has always been a work in progress. From the earliest days of scientific publishing, new findings would come along that changed the way earlier findings are understood. When research journals were published only in print, occasional errors would be reported by the authors or found by others, and papers would be retracted or corrected. When publishing became digital, many more people could quickly access and scrutinize data and images for accuracy. Now, in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), it is possible for machines to do these examinations more expeditiously and at a larger scale. All of this has added an important new layer to the publishing process and put more responsibility on authors, who must update their work if new issues arise. In response to this need, Science is improving the ways in which it will flag and notate papers that require adjustment or where changes are under consideration. Our Editorial Policies now reflect these updates.

items.title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
items.last_author_affiliation: Google Research, Mountain View, CA, USA.; Department of Physics, University of California, Santa Barbara, CA, USA.
items.abstract: Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the N -player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.

items.title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biological Chemistry and Molecular Pharmacology, Blavatnik Institute, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA.
items.abstract: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo–electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor’s ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

items.title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules
items.last_author_affiliation: Center of Materials Science and Optoelectronics Engineering, College of Materials Science and Optoelectronic Technology, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China.
items.abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900–square centimeter (cm 2 ) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm 2 ) and 21.3% for 7200-cm 2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm 2 ). The champion 7200-cm 2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.

items.title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects
items.last_author_affiliation: Ocean Ecology Lab, Marine Mammal Institute, Oregon State University, Newport, OR, USA.
items.abstract: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.

items.title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA.; Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology, Cornell University, Ithaca, NY, USA.; OWiC Technologies, Durham, NC, USA.; Kavli Institute at Cornell for Nanoscale Science, Cornell University, Ithaca, NY, USA.
items.abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.

items.title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biochemistry & Biophysics and School of Medicine and Dentistry, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY, USA.; Center for RNA Biology, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY, USA.
items.abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron–containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

items.title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
items.last_author_affiliation: Life Sciences Institute, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA.; Department of Medicinal Chemistry, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA.; Department of Chemistry, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA.; Department of Microbiology and Immunology, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA.
items.abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

items.title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress
items.last_author_affiliation: Department for Functional Neuroanatomy, Institute for Anatomy and Cell Biology, Heidelberg University, Heidelberg, Germany.; Department for General Internal Medicine, Psychosomatics and Psychotherapy, Medical Faculty Heidelberg and University Clinic Heidelberg, Heidelberg, Germany.
items.abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to–central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

items.title: Quaternary carbon–guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles
items.last_author_affiliation: Hubei Research Center of Fundamental Science-Chemistry, Engineering Research Center of Organosilicon Compounds and Materials (Ministry of Education), Hubei Key Lab on Organic and Polymeric Opto-Electronic Materials, and College of Chemistry and Molecular Sciences, Wuhan University, Wuhan, China.
items.abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

items.title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA.; Department of Civil and Environment Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA.; Institute for Medical Engineering and Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA.; Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology, Singapore.
items.abstract: Ultrasound imaging relies on soft interfaces that transmit sound efficiently between a device and the body. Conventional gel couplants provide low acoustic loss but contain mobile liquid phases that can dry, flow, or leach during extended use. By contrast, mobile phase–free elastomers are more stable but generally attenuate megahertz ultrasound strongly, limiting their use as couplants. We report an interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer molecularly designed to overcome this trade-off. A densely grafted backbone lowers the shear modulus without increasing shear loss, whereas well-packed sidechains reduce bulk compressibility, jointly suppressing acoustic attenuation in a soft elastomer. The resulting elastomer combines soft tissue–like mechanics with low-loss acoustics, providing a durable couplant for soft ultrasonic interfaces.

items.title: Angular momentum transfer from an optical vortex to an atomic rotor
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Physics, University of California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, USA.; Challenge Institute for Quantum Computation, University of California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, USA.
items.abstract: Light carries angular momentum in two forms: spin, associated with polarization, and orbital, associated with helical wavefronts. Whereas spin angular momentum underlies well-known atomic selection rules, the role of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in light-matter interaction continues to be discussed in the literature. In this work, we investigate OAM transfer from a vortex laser beam to a trapped-ion quantum rotor using rotational sidebands of the electric quadrupole transition of 40 Ca + . We directly observe coherent transfer of optical OAM into quantized rotation and identify distinct selection rules for different rotational sidebands. This observation provides experimental evidence for a scale-dependent separation of angular momentum transfer pathways in light-matter interactions. Further, our work elucidates the previously reported modified selection rules in trapped-ion experiments, establishing a unified framework for twisted light–matter interactions.

items.title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
items.last_author_affiliation: James Franck Institute and Department of Physics, University of Chicago, Chicago, IL, USA.; Enrico Fermi Institute, University of Chicago, Chicago, IL, USA.; Center for Computational Biology, Flatiron Institute, New York, NY, USA.
items.abstract: Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes turbulent fluctuations can harness ambient eddies to direct particle transport.

items.title: Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Coordination Chemistry, School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Nanjing University, Nanjing, China.; Department of Energy and Environmental Materials, Suzhou National Laboratory, Suzhou, China.; Beijing National Laboratory for Molecular Sciences, Beijing, China.
items.abstract: Aluminosilicate zeolites offer exceptional size and shape selectivity but suffer from diffusion limitations imposed by subnanometer micropores. Intrinsically meso–microporous zeolites integrate mesopores with micropores to create interconnected pathways that accelerate diffusion while preserving selectivity, yet their synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we report NJU120-5 and NJU120-7, intrinsically meso–microporous aluminosilicates that integrate micropores with mesopores enclosed by two-T-atom-thick walls containing 10-ring channels, forming a fully interconnected three-dimensional pore network. Their plausible framework models were established on the basis of advanced electron ptychographic imaging, revealing representative quasi-rectangular mesopores in calcined NJU120-5 with a uniform width of ~12 angstroms and lengths from 41 to 162 angstroms. Both materials exhibit high porosity, strong Brønsted acidity, and enhanced performance in heavy-oil cracking, delivering high yields of valuable fuels with suppressed coke formation.

items.title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Neurological Surgery, University of California, San Francisco, San Francisco, CA, USA.; Weill Institute for Neuroscience, University of California, San Francisco, San Francisco, CA, USA.; University of California, Berkeley - University of California, San Francisco Graduate Program in Bioengineering, Berkeley, CA, USA.
items.abstract: Wernicke’s area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke’s area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke’s area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

items.title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Genome Sciences, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA.; Seattle Hub for Synthetic Biology, Seattle, WA, USA.; Howard Hughes Medical Institute, Seattle, WA, USA.; Allen Institute, Seattle, WA, USA.; Brotman Baty Institute for Precision Medicine, Seattle, WA, USA.; Institute of Stem Cell and Regenerative Medicine, University of Washington; Seattle, WA, USA.; Allen Discovery Center for Cell Lineage Tracing; Seattle, WA, USA.; AI BioDesign, Seattle, WA, USA.
items.abstract: Mammalian biology unfolds over time, within tissues and organs opaque to our eyes and instruments. We applied DNA Typewriter, a sequential molecular recorder, to record the cell lineage of a mouse over nearly 2 weeks of development. From one embryo, we reconstructed a time-calibrated, parsimony-supported, zygote-rooted phylogeny of 1.28 million transcriptionally profiled cells. A burst of editing unequivocally marks the daughters of the first cleavage, which serve as inline replicates. We quantified clonal dominance arising during gastrulation. Tree siblings share cell type far above chance; heterotypic siblings mark terminal differentiations. Temporal sweeps of clade co-occurrence recover a dated hierarchy of cell type couplings; imputed labels for internal nodes recapitulate known state paths. A lineage-anchored ontogeny of mammalian development, long out of reach, is coming into view.

items.abstract: Abstract High-resolution three-dimensional (3D) tissue atlases promise to link cellular architecture to tissue function, but assembling them from serial sections containing millions of cells remains challenging. Here we present Space-map, an accurate and efficient method for reconstructing 3D tissue models from high-content spatial molecular profiles. Space-map combines multiscale feature matching with large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping to automate global alignment across serial sections while preserving local microanatomy. We generate spatial transcriptomics (Xenium; ~2.7 million cells) and proteomics (CODEX; ~4.8 million cells) datasets from serial sections to build 3D models of a colon polyp and healthy intestinal tissues. These models reveal cell-type heterogeneity in the polyp and preserved crypt and glandular architecture and mucosal-cavity continuity in healthy intestines. Benchmarking on our own and publicly available datasets demonstrates that Space-map achieves substantially higher registration accuracy and up to a tenfold speedup over existing methods, supporting its use as a robust framework for constructing 3D human tissue atlases at single-cell resolution.

4D ultrasound cerebral angiography reveals the hemodynamics of the circle of Willis in primates
items.abstract: Abstract Noninvasive imaging of hemodynamics in deep cerebral arteries is essential for understanding cerebrovascular regulation, yet remains technically challenging. Existing angiographic techniques provide structural information with limited hemodynamic characterization, whereas transcranial ultrasound is limited by skull-induced attenuation, sensitivity and restricted deep-brain coverage. We introduce four-dimensional ultrasound cerebral angiography, a noninvasive approach using MBs, for in vivo visualization and quantitative assessment of cerebral arterial hemodynamics through the intact skull. We demonstrate imaging of the circle of Willis up to 7 cm deep in nonhuman primates, with quantification of large and small vessels, over 2.5 × 3.5 × 4 cm 3 volumes, at 279-Hz volumetric rate for microbubble tracking and 151-µm spatial resolution after 3-min acquisition. This approach reveals flow organization, redistribution dynamics and interindividual variability, establishing four-dimensional ultrasound cerebral angiography as a methodological framework for deep, quantitative transcranial cerebrovascular imaging and provides a foundation for future translational development.

Characterizing the solution space of migration histories of metastatic cancers with MACH2
items.abstract: Abstract Metastases arise when cancer cells disseminate from the primary tumor, or other metastases, and seed tumors at distant anatomical sites. Reconstructing migration histories from DNA sequencing data is key to understanding the cellular mechanisms underlying metastatic dissemination. While the data often support many equally plausible histories, current methods return a single solution or sample alternatives without guarantees of optimality or completeness. Here we introduce MACH2, which enumerates all optimal migration histories and summarizes them to identify high-confidence migrations. MACH2 combines existing parsimony criteria with a new criterion that minimizes the number of clones assigned to locations where they were not observed, and includes MACH2-viz, an interactive tool for exploring solutions. Using simulated tumors with known ground truth, we show that MACH2 outperforms existing methods. Across 145 lung, ovarian, breast and prostate cancers, MACH2 reveals extensive uncertainty in migration histories, infers histories consistent with orthogonal experimental data, and finds metastasis-to-metastasis seeding and linear progression to be common.

Optimizing phenotype scale improves genetic analyses in large-scale biobanks
items.abstract: Abstract Large-scale biobanks have enabled increasingly complicated genetic analyses across thousands of phenotypes. However, studies rarely consider the appropriateness of the phenotype scale, which can drastically affect inference on genetic architecture. Here we introduce SIQReg, which learns a data-driven phenotype scale by minimizing heterogeneity across phenotype quantiles. Across 25 UK Biobank complex traits, SIQReg rejects the default scale for 24. Generally, SIQReg scales lie between default and logarithmic, indicating that traits are neither purely additive nor purely multiplicative. SIQReg improves both nonadditive and additive genetic analyses. It eliminates most nonadditive signals, including 97% of variance quantitative trait loci, indicating that they may be scale-induced, while preserving biologically plausible nonadditive signals. It simultaneously improves power for additive signals, increasing identification of genome-wide association loci and transcriptome-wide association genes by 11% and 13%, respectively, improving polygenic prediction accuracy by 10%, and identifying 50% more high-risk individuals. These gains are replicated across ancestry groups. Our results establish SIQReg as a principled phenotype scale transformation approach that improves genetic analyses of complex traits.

Harnessing regioselective aryl migration of pyridone-based aryl-λ3-iodonium salts to access iodine-substituted aryloxypyridines
items.abstract: Abstract While 2- and 4-aryloxypyridines are ubiquitous in pharmaceutical molecules, efficient synthetic strategies—especially for synthesizing scaffolds with diverse multiple substituents on the pyridine core—remain limited. Here we show a hook-and-slide strategy for constructing these scaffolds, involving the in-situ generation of pyridonyl(aryl)iodonium salts from pyridones and Koser’s reagent (hook, C3 selectivity), followed by an iodine-to-oxygen aryl migration (slide, O selectivity). Such newly designed iodonium salts feature dual vicinal nucleophilic sites, and we demonstrate that using C2 − H imidazolium ionic liquids can exclusively transfer the aryl group to the strategic O site. This approach is transition-metal-free, scalable, and applicable to substrates with diverse electronic and steric properties or complex structures. Importantly, the resulting products retain −I and −NH 2 handles that are amenable to downstream derivatizations, enabling extensive exploration of previously inaccessible chemical space. The utility of this approach is further demonstrated through the concise synthesis of multiple pharmaceutical intermediates and a CRF 1 antagonist, CP-376395.

items.title: Greenland ice sheet retreat intensifies the African monsoon through a polar-tropical atmospheric teleconnection
items.abstract: Abstract Global climate forcing drives major changes in the North African summer monsoon (NASM), yet how high-latitude cryospheric changes influence tropical hydroclimate through atmospheric dynamics remains unclear. Integrating paleoclimate proxy evidence with coupled climate-model simulations, sensitivity experiments, and idealized atmospheric modeling, we show that Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) retreat acts as a dynamically important amplifier of NASM rainfall. Using the mid-Pliocene as a natural experiment for sustained global warming, we find that NASM rainfall was markedly stronger than that simulated under transient future warming for comparable global-mean temperature increases. GrIS retreat enhances Arctic warming, thereby perturbing the upper-tropospheric westerly jet and triggering a stationary Rossby wave train linking Greenland to North Africa. This polar–tropical atmospheric teleconnection strengthens monsoon circulation and moisture convergence, producing wetter conditions across the Sahara–Sahel. These results reveal a high-latitude pathway through which slow cryospheric changes modulate low-latitude monsoon variability under sustained warming.

items.title: Evolutionary plasticity of bacterial surface layer protein exoskeletons
items.abstract: Abstract All cellular life possesses environmental interfaces like cell membranes or cell walls, yet the compositional complexity of these major cell components limits structural and evolutionary studies. Prokaryotic surface layer (S-layer) exoskeletons, with their homopolymer paracrystalline architecture, offer a more tractable model of an environmental interface. However, extreme sequence diversity and heterogeneous multidomain organisation of S-layer proteins confound conventional evolutionary analyses. Here, by combining phylogenomics with structural modelling, we show that extensive sequence divergence, modular evolution and lateral gene transfer drive lineage-specific S-layer diversification across both monoderm ( Bacillaceae , Peptostreptococcaceae ) and diderm ( Caulobacteraceae , Deinococcaceae ) bacteria. Focusing on the Gram-positive order Peptostreptococcales , including environmental isolates and clinical pathogens, we uncover multiple S-layer architectures conferring divergent physiological properties. Molecular microbiology reveals that among close relatives utilising the same exoskeleton type, only pathogens display resistance to the antimicrobial immune effectors LL-37 and lysozyme. Furthermore, by experimentally determining two S-layer structures, we unravel how mechanisms including (intra)domain gains and losses generate hyper-diversity of homologous S-layers among clinical isolates of the pathogen Clostridioides difficile . Our findings establish the S-layer as a paradigm of molecular modularity and evolutionary plasticity. Specifically, evolution of a single structural protein enables rapid cell-surface reconfiguration and contributes to immune evasion in bacterial pathogens.

items.title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
items.abstract: Abstract Coexisting populations performing similar functions (i.e., functional redundancy), can stabilize ecosystem outputs under disturbance. The insurance hypothesis proposes that diversity maintains community function under disturbance because functionally redundant taxa differ in their environmental responsiveness. However, how redundancy and insurance interact in microbial communities remains unclear. Here, we examine functional redundancy and insurance potential in soil microbial communities under long-term heat disturbance from an underground coal seam fire in Centralia, Pennsylvania, USA, using seven years of deep metagenome sequencing across heated and reference sites. Functional redundancy increases with disturbance intensity, driven by declines in taxonomic diversity and average genome size and by increased per-genome investment in biogeochemically relevant metabolisms (i.e., carbohydrate and nitrogen). However, a proposed proxy for environmental responsiveness, transcription factor evenness, is reduced in heated soils. These results indicate that prolonged, selective disturbance can enhance redundancy while simultaneously constraining insurance against future stress, shaping microbial community resilience under persistent disturbance.

items.title: A metal ion-assisted workflow for practical and scalable enrichment of small extracellular vesicles from biofluids
Facial photographs reveal mortality risk beyond triage and clinical risk scores
Early face-experience deprivation leads to long-lasting deficits in macaque cortical face processing
items.abstract: Abstract Experience-dependent plasticity in early sensory cortex is restricted to critical periods early in development. Whether plasticity in higher-order cortex is similarly restricted remains unclear. In the primate ventral visual stream, face-selective cortex emerges with experience during development, providing a powerful system to test how the timing of experience shapes higher-order representations. Using three male rhesus macaques selectively deprived of early face experience followed by prolonged normal face exposure, we found that face-experience-deprived monkeys acquire face-directed viewing behavior and neural face selectivity. However, they showed atypical within-face viewing patterns, while their neural representations retained lasting signatures of early deprivation, including selectivity for both faces and hands and reduced discrimination for face identity, expression, and viewpoint. Thus, higher-order visual cortex remains plastic beyond early development, yet the timing of experience fundamentally constrains the refinement of later-acquired neural representations.

items.title: Interfacial mechanisms of gas-bubble friction
In vivo programming of dual-targeted CAR-T cells facilitates vascular disruption and T-cell infiltration in solid tumors
Impacts of medications for obesity on global health and the environment
items.abstract: Abstract A new generation of medications for obesity could transform the global food system. While research has explored their health impacts, their implications for global food demand and land use remain unquantified. We apply a global food system model to project the impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1) uptake to 2050 among people with obesity under two scenarios: reduced calorie intake while maintaining dietary composition, and reduced calorie intake combined with shifts towards the EAT–Lancet diet. Compared with the Reference scenario, GLP-1-mediated calorie reduction alone results in up to 6.6 million avoided deaths globally in 2050 and 32 Mha more natural land area, reflecting reductions in cropland, pasture and managed forest. Combining GLP-1 use with EAT–Lancet dietary shifts increases these estimates to 7.7 million avoided deaths and 46 Mha more natural land. Lower food prices increase food consumption among untreated populations, including unhealthy foods, partially offsetting these gains.

items.title: Protecting-group-lean platform for synthesizing diverse phenylethanoid glycosides uncovers antifibrotic leads
items.abstract: Abstract Phenylethanoid glycosides are structurally diverse natural products widely found in traditional medicinal plants and display a broad range of biological activities. However, systematic studies of their functions and structure–activity relationships have been limited by inefficient access to diverse analogs in useful quantities. Here we show a protecting-group-lean synthetic platform that provides a 29-member library of phenylethanoid glycosides with variations at four positions of the central glucose unit. The strategy combines regioselective glycosylation, β-selective glycosylation without neighboring-group assistance, selective caffeoylation, and a mild global deprotection that preserves labile caffeoyl esters. Two glycosylations and two additional transformations can be performed sequentially in one pot, substantially streamlining assembly. Biological evaluation in a TGF-β-induced fibroblast model reveals structure–activity relationships, provides insight into signaling pathways associated with antifibrotic activity, and identifies several compounds as promising leads for further antifibrotic studies.

items.title: Trypanosomes Maintain Propulsion in Confined Environments by Modulating Rotational Motility from Swimming to Network-Threading Propulsion
items.abstract: Abstract The parasite Trypanosoma brucei lives in the body fluids of its hosts, including blood and interstitial fluids of various tissues. The mechanism of dissemination within these environments remains largely unresolved, although the trypanosome´s motility is known to play an essential role for its survival. The unicellular flagellate is a versatile microswimmer, like bacteria or sperm cells, albeit structurally more complex than these classical models. Here we study their motility in different viscous and elastic regimes. Using quantitative high speed video microscopy and digital holography microscopy, we detail the three-dimensional mechanical reaction of the flexible cell body with its uniquely attached flagellum to increasing confinement, leading to a network-threading type propulsion. This allows stable progressive motility despite a reduction in wave parameters up to tissue-like confinement. We thus show how trypanosomes can mechanically adjust in response to various microenvironments and, using flagellar beat reversal, manage the exploration of their complex environments.

Parental leave benefits and fathers’ postpartum mental health in Sweden
items.abstract: Abstract Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers’ mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. Using national population registers, we include 210,285 first-time fathers whose children were born between 2007 and 2011. Fathers receiving basic benefits have higher odds of receiving any mental healthcare, being prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics, and using specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related benefits. The results are robust after adjusting for mental health history, income and employment status, though associations are attenuated. Fathers who do not take parental leave during the first year are more likely to receive any mental healthcare, specialist outpatient care or hospitalisation. Overall, fathers with access to more generous paid parental leave benefits experience better postpartum mental health. These findings suggest that well-compensated parental leave may benefit fathers’ mental health and promote gender equality in caregiving. However, further efforts are needed to determine whether parental leave systems mitigate or reproduce health inequalities given that parental leave benefit levels are contingent on labour market conditions.

items.title: Numerosity is directly sensed and dynamically transformed in the human brain
Bordetella pertussis adapts to human nasal mucosa through biofilm-associated virulence reprogramming and host-defense attenuation
Droplet-Assisted Growth of Re-Entrant Micro-Mushroom Surfaces with Switchable Superhydrophobicity and Adhesive Resistance
items.abstract: Abstract Nature-inspired designs for surface micro- and nanostructures have long attracted attention for their potential multifunctionality. This study introduces a mushroom-shaped silicone re-entrant structure achieved through a one-step, in-situ dynamic Droplet-Assisted Growth and Shaping strategy. The unique shape and multicomponent hybrid properties of the inert rod base and chemically modifiable spherical head of these silicone micro-mushrooms (SMMs) provide exceptional surface wetting and adhesion characteristics. The engineered single-scale rough surface exhibits the remarkable rose petal effect, featuring a water contact angle exceeding 150° and demonstrating extraordinary water adhesion. The wetting states of these surfaces can be easily altered through O 2 -plasma treatment with the reconstruction of secondary and tertiary hierarchical nanostructures. This approach also effectively converts petal-effect surfaces into lotus-effect surfaces, significantly enhancing their self-cleaning performance. Furthermore, the SMM coatings display extremely low adhesion to various adhesives, including tapes, hot glue, and all-purpose adhesives, with pull-off forces nearing 0. This characteristic ensures a smooth detachment from sticky surfaces. The durability of the SMM structures is noteworthy, as they maintain their morphology even after 1,000 loop tack tests and can endure 8.7 MPa compression and 500 cycles of linear abrasion on sticky surfaces.

items.title: Asymmetric coordination triggers dual-site synergy in gold nanoclusters for efficient aerobic oxidation
Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BOx catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation
items.abstract: Abstract The oxidative dehydrogenation of propane offers a promising route to propylene, but developing low-temperature catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a Co@BO x inverse catalyst featuring engineered defects localized at face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter. Using an oxidative atmosphere-induced exsolution strategy, we continuously tune the face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase ratio, maximizing the density of stacking faults at a 1:1 phase ratio. Catalytic activity exhibits a strong positive correlation with stacking fault density, with the optimal Co F/H-1.0 @BO x catalyst achieving 32% propane conversion and 83% olefin selectivity at 450 °C—5.1 times that of pristine cobalt boride. Density functional theory reveals that stacking faults modulate Co atomic spacing, weakening the excessively strong BO x -Co interfacial interaction. In situ spectroscopy demonstrates that maximized stacking faults strengthen O-H bonds in surface boron hydroxyl species and optimize radical initiation kinetics. This work establishes subsurface defect engineering as a potential strategy to enhance oxide overlayer reactivity in inverse catalytic systems.

items.title: Quantum sensing-enabled deuterium NMR spectroscopy with nanoscale sensitivity at low magnetic fields
items.abstract: Abstract Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unparalleled access to molecular structure and dynamics but is traditionally limited by weak signal strength, requiring large sample volumes and high magnetic fields. Here, we demonstrate nanoscale deuterium ( 2 H) NMR spectroscopy using nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, yielding characteristic quadrupolar powder line shapes that are present in conventional bulk NMR spectra. By detecting statistical spin fluctuations from nanometer-scale detection volumes, our approach delivers a sensitivity enhancement of seven to eight orders of magnitude in terms of spin sensitivity over inductive detection, while operating at magnetic fields two orders of magnitude lower than those used in conventional NMR. Temperature-dependent measurements of a deuterated polymer and a molecular solid reveal distinct motional averaging and phase transitions with nanoscale sensitivity. Powder-like NV-detected 2 H NMR establishes a powerful tool for probing molecular dynamics on the nanoscale - capabilities beyond those of most existing spectroscopic techniques.

items.title: Vertically aligned dual-channel metal-organic framework nanosheet membranes for gas separation
Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels
items.abstract: Abstract Metal fuels are central to energetic materials because of their high energy density and intense heat-release capability. However, early-stage formation of passivating oxide shells severely restricts oxygen diffusion, resulting in incomplete oxidation and limited energy utilization. Here, we report a Ce-assisted microstructure design strategy to overcome this long-standing diffusion barrier by constructing three-dimensional oxygen-diffusion scaffolds within aluminum-based fuels through trace cerium addition. Rapidly solidified Al– x Ce powders develop an interconnected Al 11 Ce 3 network, which subdivides the Al matrix into fine domains. During heating and combustion, this Al 11 Ce 3 network is preferentially oxidized into a CeO 2- x /CeO 2 -containing scaffold before extensive Al oxidation, thereby providing continuous oxygen-transport pathways into the particle interior. As a result, Al– x Ce alloy powders exhibit shorter ignition delay, faster flame propagation, shorter combustion duration, and more complete oxidation than pure Al. This work establishes a general and scalable design principle for enhancing metal-fuel combustion through rare-earth-enabled oxygen-diffusion networks.

items.title: Rapid and selective metal-free O2 reduction to H2O2 using a molecular CpN3 electrocatalyst
Macrophage-exacerbated viral lung injury and mechanical overdistension-driven bacterial superinfection replicated in a human lung chip
Hybrid-parity sliding multiferroics
Lanthanide-dependent methanotroph thrives on radioactive promethium
authors: Huub J. M. Op den Camp
items.abstract: Abstract Lanthanides serve as essential cofactors in the methanol dehydrogenases of methylotrophic bacteria. While biological function has been characterized for the naturally occurring members of the series, promethium, the only lanthanide existing as exclusively radioactive isotopes and virtually absent from nature, has remained unexplored. Here, the acidophilic methanotroph Methylacidiphilum fumariolicum SolV grows on β⁻-emitting Pm-147 as its sole lanthanide source, removing 98% of the isotope from the medium over 60 h despite a calculated radiation dose of 3.6 Gy. Reconstituted methanol dehydrogenase of the type XoxF -MDH displays Pm-dependent activity precisely between the neodymium and samarium variants. Bacterial lanthanide metabolism thus incorporates a naturally absent and radioactive member of the lanthanide series.

items.title: Mitigating brittleness in ceramics via transformation- and twinning-induced plasticity
items.abstract: Abstract Ceramics usually exhibit inherent brittleness at room temperature due to their strong covalent/ionic bonding and few active slip systems. Consequently, ceramics exhibit a low damage-bearing capacity and typically sudden failure prior to yielding. Thus, achieving room-temperature plasticity while maintaining or enhancing the strength of ceramics remains critical and challenging. Here, we report a promising strategy to address this problem by concurrently activating twinning-induced plasticity and transformation-induced plasticity in a monolithic TaN ceramic film. Through precisely controlled physical vapor deposition, we stabilize the metastable δ-TaN phase with hierarchical nanotwinned architectures. Then, by combining micromechanical tests, atomic-resolution characterization, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that the synergy of phase transformation and twinning brings exceptional damage tolerance and plasticity, achieving up to 60% compressive strain without catastrophic fracture alongside a hardness of ~43 GPa. Our work not only proves the feasibility of twinning and transformation-induced plasticity synergy in designing ultrahard and ductile materials, but also highlights the architecture optimization in nanotwinned ceramics.

items.title: Coherence toroidal vortices and statistic-veiled correlation topologies
items.abstract: Abstract Toroidal vortices in fluid and gas dynamics underpin a broad spectrum of scientific and technological fields, from elementary particle physics to condensed matter systems, and have recently garnered significant attention in optics because of their inherent topological stability. Here we report the experimental observation of toroidal vortices in stochastic optical wavefields with partial coherence, termed coherence toroidal vortices, which eliminates deterministic topological signatures in conventional optical degrees of freedom while unveiling statistically hidden correlation topologies. These underlying topologies—including both fundamental and higher-order hopfionic textures—emerge in second-order field correlations and are accessible only through statistical measurements. We further examine the impact of chaotic channels on the stability of these statistically veiled correlation topologies, demonstrating that their topological invariants remain robust under realistic environmental perturbations. These findings are experimentally validated and offer novel insights into the potential of toroidal light vortices serving as controllable channels for directional energy and information transfer within complex media.

items.title: Large electrocaloric effects in unannealed multilayer capacitors of partially ordered lead scandium tantalate
items.abstract: Abstract Multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 with good B-site cation order ( S 111 ~ 0.9-0.96) are driven by supercritical fields of 15.8 V μm −1 in prototype coolers, such that large electrocaloric effects arise over a wide range of temperatures and peak to give thermocouple-measured temperature jumps of |∆ T j | ~ 4.0 K near room temperature. However, the high degree of B-site order requires an energetically expensive 42-day high-temperature anneal that would be economically expensive and environmentally damaging in mass production. Here we report that the performance reduction (4.0 K → 3.1 K) for unannealed multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 with partial B-site order ( S 111 ~ 0.6) is surprisingly small because reduced latent heat is mitigated by high-field electrocaloric effects in the induced ferroelectric phase. Eliminating the anneal without unduly compromising performance should render unannealed multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 attractive for applications.

items.title: Symmetry-breaking antibody binding reveals extensive capsid malleability in pandemic human norovirus
Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI
Hyperelastic microfibers as bioinspired proprioceptive artificial muscles
items.abstract: Abstract Skeletal muscles combine forceful contraction with built-in sensing of their own length and movement, known as proprioception. Reproducing this combination in soft artificial muscles remains difficult, because added sensors often reduce actuation performance, complicate fabrication or limit miniaturization. In natural muscle, specialized sensory fibers are embedded alongside, and mechanically coupled to, the force-generating fibers. Inspired by this arrangement, we pair a hyperelastic, highly stretchable fluid channel with a stiffer, off-center optical core inside a single thin fiber. When liquid is pumped in, the channel wall undergoes a shape bifurcation: a localized bulge forms and propagates along the fiber. Because the core resists stretching, the bulge bends the fiber into a contracting coil, while the core also reports the fiber’s shape through the light it transmits. Here we show that such fibers, produced continuously by a scalable drawing process, act as artificial muscles that sense their own contraction and stretching, supporting self-monitoring movement in soft robots.

Benchmarking computational tools for locus-specific analysis of transposable elements in single-cell RNA-seq datasets
items.abstract: Abstract Background Transposable elements (TEs) are increasingly recognized as regulators of gene expression and cellular identity. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables the analysis of their transcription at cellular resolution, but the repetitive nature of TEs and their frequent overlap with genes create substantial mapping ambiguity. Although several tools quantify TE expression, few support locus-specific analysis, and their performance in single-cell data has not been systematically evaluated. Results We present a comprehensive, scalable benchmarking framework written in Snakemake for locus-level TE quantification in short-read scRNA-seq data, combining real datasets with simulations that provide read-level ground truth. Our simulations show that sequence-diverged insertions can be quantified with relatively high accuracy, whereas young TEs remain difficult to resolve due to unreliable assignment of multi-mapping reads. We observe pronounced family-specific biases and identify gene-TE disambiguation as a major unresolved challenge. Across the evaluated methods, incorporating multi-mapping reads generally increased false-positive calls without substantially improving locus-level accuracy. When loci of all ages were analyzed together, SoloTE in unique-mapper mode achieved the highest detection accuracy. Conclusions Our benchmark delineates the fundamental limits imposed by short-read scRNA-seq on locus-specific TE quantification, providing practical guidance for prospective users. Suggested best practices include focusing locus-level analyses on older insertions, applying unique-mapper strategies to improve precision, aggregating counts at the subfamily level for young TEs, and explicitly checking for gene-TE overlaps. Our workflow is reproducible and extensible, providing a foundation for evaluating emerging methods aimed at resolving TE transcription at single-locus resolution.

items.title: Dynamic changes in mRNA isoform usage during human retinal organoid development
Adding layers of information to scRNA-seq data using pre-trained language models
items.abstract: Abstract Pre-trained language models promise to enrich single-cell analyses with contextual information from large biomedical text corpora, but it remains unclear how to optimally align this knowledge with quantitative single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. To address this, we construct text-based training datasets from both scRNA-seq data and biomedical literature targeted to the experimental setting at hand. We then fine-tune lightweight encoder-only biomedical language models to learn a shared, literature-enriched representation. Controlled evaluations across immune and developmental datasets show that this representation preserves cell identity while adding robust and interpretable contextual layers of functional, disease-associated, and developmental information to single-cell analysis workflows.

items.title: SPiCe: integrative spatial modelling of cellular plasticity using graph neural networks and geostatistics
items.abstract: Abstract Cellular plasticity, the ability of cells to change phenotype in response to intrinsic and environmental cues, is central to development and disease, yet remains difficult to quantify. We present SPiCe, a framework that integrates graph neural networks and spatial regression models to predict and explain cell state variation in spatial transcriptomics data. Applied to epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity (EMP) in breast cancer, SPiCe shows that mesenchymal states are stabilised by copy number alterations and microenvironmental cues, whereas hybrid states remain unpredictable, and uncovers long-range myofibroblast influences on EMP. Together, these analyses provide a framework for quantifying cellular plasticity and its spatial determinants.
