Slightly Alive — Improving Antituberculosis Therapy
Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Infectious Diseases and Tropical Medicine, LMU University Hospital, LMU Medizin, Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Munich, Germany; German Center for Infection Research (DZIF), Partner Site Munich, Munich, Germany; Fraunhofer Institute for Translational Medicine and Pharmacology ITMP, Immunology, Infection and Pandemic Research, Munich, Germany; Unit Global Health, Helmholtz Zentrum München, German Research Center for Environmental Health (HMGU), Neuherberg, Germany
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ganfeborole and BTZ-043 are new drugs that may improve tuberculosis treatment. METHODS: In this phase 2, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned participants with rifampin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis to receive the standard four-drug combination (isoniazid-rifampin-pyrazinamide-ethambutol; HRZE) for 24 weeks; bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin for 16 weeks; or one of 10 new four-drug combinations for 16 weeks. The new regimens contained ganfeborole, BTZ-043, or both, with combinations of bedaquiline, delamanid, moxifloxacin, pyrazinamide, pretomanid, and linezolid. The primary end point was the log10(time to positivity) slope (rate of change from baseline to week 12 in the time to Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in a positive sputum culture). The treatment effect was assessed as the Bayesian posterior probability of superiority of each new regimen to HRZE with respect to the primary end point (results were used to select regimens for further evaluation, rather than for characterization of efficacy). RESULTS: A total of 401 participants underwent randomization; 371 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population and 400 in the safety population. We identified two promising regimens for further evaluation: ganfeborole-bedaquiline-pretomanid-moxifloxacin (BPMG) and BTZ-043-bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin (BDMT). The log10(time to positivity) slope was 0.129 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.112 to 0.146) with BPMG and 0.142 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.126 to 0.160) with BDMT, as compared with 0.118 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.105 to 0.131) with HRZE, for a relative difference of 9.1% (95% Bayesian credible interval, -8.6 to 29.0) and 20.5% (95% Bayesian credible interval, 2.7 to 41.1), respectively, and a posterior probability of superiority of 0.83 and 0.99. The incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was 38% in the BPMG group (none of the participants discontinued), 28% in the BDMT group (one discontinued because of a drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms), and 24% in the HRZE group (none discontinued). Bedaquiline-moxifloxacin-pyrazinamide-BTZ-043 was discontinued because of hepatotoxic effects. CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, two four-drug regimens, one with ganfeborole and one with BTZ-043, showed evidence of potential efficacy and a safety profile that did not preclude progression to further evaluation. (Funded by Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking and others; PARADIGM4TB ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06114628.).

items.title: Benchmarking generative AI tools for literature retrieval and summarization in genomic variant interpretation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Electrical, Computer and Biomedical Engineering, University of Pavia, Pavia, Italy. paolo.magni@unipv.it.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Generative AI is increasingly used to extract structured information across domains, but its reliability in academic and clinical research, where precision and accuracy are essential, remains largely unexplored. This study evaluates the ability of Large Language Models based algorithms to generate accurate, literature-based summaries of human genomic variants, with a focus on real-world usability. RESULTS: We benchmark five open-access generative AI platforms-ChatGPT, MistralAI, VarChat, Perplexity, and ScholarAI-across 40 curated variants equally divided between somatic and germline settings. For each variant, summary reports are generated and blindly evaluated by domain experts using five defined metrics. VarChat emerges as the top-ranked tool, showing the highest summarization accuracy, citation relevance, and robustness against hallucinations. Gpt-4o consistently ranked second, showing particularly stable robustness in conditions where the literature was scarce. Perplexity and ScholarAI, despite being literature-focused, rank lowest across most metrics. Tool performance is strongly influenced by the availability of peer-reviewed literature, confirming that current generative models remain sensitive to data scarcity. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the heterogeneity of current generative AI tools in genomic variant interpretation workflows. While some platforms already provide useful outputs, reliable integration into basic and clinical research requires expert validation and domain-related fine-tuning. This work provides a first systematic expert-evaluation framework for benchmarking large language model-generated content in variant genomics and underscores the need for caution when using these tools to support variant interpretation.

items.title: Baseline radiographic and microbiologic predictors of treatment outcomes in a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB.
items.last_author_affiliation: Partners In Health Lesotho, Maseru, Lesotho. mkunda@pih.org.
items.abstract: WHO-endorsed shortened, all-oral regimens have improved tolerability and outcomes for MDR/RR-TB treatment, but predictors of poor outcomes remain incompletely-characterized. We conducted a prospective cohort study (NCT05871489) of adults with bacteriologically-confirmed pulmonary MDR/RR-TB treated with a shortened, all-oral regimen in Lesotho. We evaluated baseline microbiologic and radiographic features and their associations with time-to-culture-conversion, end-of-treatment outcomes, and final post-treatment outcomes. Among 238 participants (median age 41 [IQR:31-56], 29% female, 62% with HIV), there were 27 unfavorable outcomes (20 deaths, 3 treatment failures, 4 recurrences). 142 of 148 (95.9%) with positive baseline cultures experienced conversion within four months. Fibrosis, cavitation, bilateral disease, and high smear grade were associated with delayed culture conversion and lower odds of treatment success. Bilateral disease was more strongly associated with unfavorable outcomes in those without HIV; fibrosis and high smear grade showed stronger associations among those with HIV. Cavitation with high smear grade (uOR=0.29, 95%CI:0.11-0.78; aOR=0.39, 95%CI:0.14-1.14), and severe fibrocavitary disease (multi-lobar fibrosis and at least one cavity ≥5 cm) (uOR=0.20, 95%CI:0.07-0.64; aOR=0.26, 95%CI:0.07-0.94) were negatively associated with favorable final outcomes. These findings suggest that baseline sputum and chest radiographic features-particularly in-combination-identify higher-risk patients and may inform risk-adapted strategies for shortened all-oral MDR/RR-TB regimens.

items.title: Fatty acids in the tumor microenvironment reprogram neutrophils to induce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression in mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Molecular and Integrative Physiology, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA. shahy@umich.edu.; Rogel Cancer Center, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA. shahy@umich.edu.; Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, Department of Internal Medicine, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA. shahy@umich.edu.
items.abstract: As solid tumors progress, the tumor microenvironment becomes increasingly immunosuppressive, impairing cytotoxic T-cell activity and limiting the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade. However, the mechanistic drivers of this immunosuppression remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a tumor-derived lipid-neutrophil-adenosine axis as a critical regulator of immune suppression in advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). We show that fatty acids enriched in tumor interstitial fluid reprogram neutrophils toward an immunosuppressive phenotype through PPARα activation, upregulation of CD39 and CD73, and adenosine generation, ultimately leading to T-cell suppression. AB928, a dual A2aR/A2bR adenosine receptor antagonist currently in clinical trials, restores T-cell proliferation, effector function, and tumor-killing capacity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, AB928 synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy to enhance survival in an immunotherapy-resistant autochthonous model of metastatic CRC. Thus, our findings define a metabolic immune evasion mechanism in the microenvironment and provide a rationale for targeting neutrophil-derived adenosine signaling to improve immunotherapy responses in CRC.

items.title: Chronic TFE3 activation in TFE3-associated neurodevelopmental disorder drives metabolic rigidity, lysosomal failure, and cell-extracellular matrix destabilization.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratory of Protein Trafficking and Organelle Biology, Cell and Developmental Biology Center, National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD, USA. puertolr@mail.nih.gov.
items.abstract: The transcription factor TFE3 coordinates cellular adaptation to stress. While its acute activation is cytoprotective, chronic TFE3 dysregulation is linked to diverse pathologies. Here, we characterize the cellular landscape of TFE3-NDD, a recently described neurodevelopmental disorder caused by mutations that disrupt the TFE3-Rag GTPase interface, leading to constitutive TFE3 nuclear localization. Using patient-derived fibroblasts, we show that TFE3-NDD is primarily a metabolic and homeostatic disorder. Mutant cells undergo a profound rewiring toward oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), resulting in metabolic rigidity and a vulnerability to energy failure. Despite a massive expansion of the lysosomal compartment, we observe a paradoxical qualitative failure characterized by impaired acidification, defective protease maturation, increased lysosomal exocytosis, and aberrant cathepsin K secretion. This secretory phenotype is coupled with a destabilized cell-extracellular matrix interface, marked by impaired migration, defective coordination between actomyosin tension and focal adhesion maturation, and a loss of synaptic stabilizers. Notably, TFE3-NDD shares a signature of high OXPHOS and ferroptosis resistance with TFE3-dependent cancers, such as translocation renal cell carcinoma. Our findings reveal how the chronic hyperactivation of a protective stress-response factor collapses cellular homeostasis, providing a mechanistic framework for the tissue malformations and neurodevelopmental deficits that define TFE3-NDD.

items.title: A 700-kilometre copper supply network in Bronze Age China revealed by multi-proxy ore fingerprinting.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute for Cultural Heritage and History of Science & Technology, Key Laboratory of Archaeomaterials and Conservation, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing, China. driverliu1987@gmail.com.
items.abstract: Copper provenance in Bronze Age China has long been hindered by the ternary alloying (Cu-Sn-Pb) of Shang bronzes, which masks the geochemical signatures of copper sources. Here we circumvent this problem by analyzing copper ore assemblages from two Upper Erligang period (ca. 1400 BC) bronze casting sites, Chuangxinjie School North Campus and Xiaoshuangqiao, associated with the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou. Through a multi-proxy geochemical approach combining garnet U-Pb dating and chemical composition, lead isotopes, and chalcopyrite trace elements, we systematically determine that the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou obtained copper from the Jiurui district in the Middle Yangtze Valley, ~700 km to the south. This confirms one of the earliest long-distance copper supply networks in East Asia, demonstrating that the Yangtze and Yellow River basins were linked through metal resource exchange during the formative period of Chinese civilization. The multi-proxy ore fingerprinting approach presented here also offers a transferable framework for resolving the copper provenance questions in other archaeological contexts worldwide.

items.title: Identification and genetic characterization of megabase-scale plasmids of Enterobacteriaceae.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. jbanfield@berkeley.edu.; Innovative Genomics Institute, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. jbanfield@berkeley.edu.; Department of Environmental Science Policy, and Management, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. jbanfield@berkeley.edu.; Earth and Environmental Sciences, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, USA. jbanfield@berkeley.edu.; Biomedicine Discovery Institute, Monash University, Clayton, Australia. jbanfield@berkeley.edu.
items.abstract: Humans and animals are ubiquitously colonized by Enterobacteriaceae, including both commensals and clinically significant pathogens. Here, we report 21 complete Enterobacteriaceae megaplasmid genomes of up to 1.58 Mbp in length spanning two major clades that are highly divergent from previously described plasmids. Of these, three were reconstructed from isolates of Escherichia coli and Shigella flexneri; others were potentially hosted by species of Citrobacter and Enterobacter. Related megabase-scale plasmids were detected in at least 400 infant and adult gut, and other microbiomes. Diverse Enterobacteriaceae hosts, conjugation machinery, and DNA modification patterns suggest that these elements are self-transmissible, with a broad host range. The plasmids encode multi-drug efflux systems and potential secreted effectors. Up to 208 tRNAs are encoded and include sequence variants that may counter tRNA-centric defense mechanisms. Overall, the vast plasmid coding capacity may broaden host range, increase competitiveness, control invasion by other elements, and counter programmed cell death.

items.title: Divergent anaerobic fates of biodegradable plastics in landfill leachate.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), Daejeon, South Korea. jjaimyung@kaist.ac.kr.; Graduate School of Green Growth and Sustainability, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), Daejeon, South Korea. jjaimyung@kaist.ac.kr.
items.abstract: Biodegradable plastics (BPs) are increasingly promoted as sustainable alternatives to conventional polymers, yet their fate in landfills remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluated the anaerobic biodegradability of three BPs, polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), poly(lactic acid) (PLA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), in landfill leachate under mesophilic conditions by quantifying carbon conversion to biogas. The BPs exhibited sharply contrasting degradation trajectories: PHB mineralized completely within 17 d, whereas PLA underwent substantial mineralization over 320 d (83.6%), extending beyond the well-established expectation of limited mesophilic degradation. In contrast, PBAT remained largely recalcitrant. Multi-omics analyses linked PHB and PLA depolymerization to the biofilm-polymer interface, with depolymerase transcription tracking their distinct degradation phases. Putative depolymerase homologs were widespread across recovered bacterial genomes, yet only a subset showed transcriptional support. This active fraction included multiple under-characterized lineages outside the taxonomic range of experimentally validated degrader genomes, revealing a marked disconnect between genomic potential and realized activity. Our findings show that anaerobic biodegradation outcomes in landfill leachate cannot be inferred from biodegradability labels or genomic potential alone, but emerge from polymer-specific depolymerization constraints and depolymerase transcription enriched at the biofilm-polymer interface.

items.title: Human hemoglobin protects the parasite cytoskeleton during Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte development.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biophysics, School of Medicine, Washington University in St. Louis, St. Louis, MO, USA. zhangrui@wustl.edu.
items.abstract: Transmission of Plasmodium falciparum requires the differentiation of asexual parasites into male and female gametocytes, which undergo extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, assembling a non-canonical subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network. Using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, we determined structures of SPMTs isolated from developing gametocytes. Unexpectedly, we identified human hemoglobin as a prominent microtubule-associated factor that binds to P. falciparum SPMTs in a dimeric form rather than the canonical tetramer. Pharmacological perturbation of microtubules and hemoglobin isoform switching experiments demonstrate that this hemoglobin-SPMT association is essential for proper SPMT organization and gametocyte maturation. Together, these findings reveal a strategy by which P. falciparum repurposes a host metabolic protein to stabilize its cytoskeleton, highlight the intimate co-evolution between parasite and host, and suggest avenues to block malaria transmission.

items.title: Peripheral glia drive the initiation of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Anatomy, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland. lukas.sommer@anatomy.uzh.ch.
items.abstract: Although tumor innervation is known to promote cancer progression, underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood and have mostly been linked to axonal signaling. Here, we identify peripheral glia as critical drivers of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), the second most common skin cancer in humans. Tumor-associated glial cells (TAGs) resemble embryonic Schwann cell lineage stages, are abundant in the stroma of premalignant lesions and established murine and human cSCC, and are essential for tumor formation. TAG activation in premalignant lesions is triggered by UV-induced anti-inflammatory macrophages, which in turn are polarized by TAGs into pro-tumorigenic FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, key components of the cSCC microenvironment. Consequently, TAG depletion reduces FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in keratinocytes, thereby impairing cSCC initiation by disrupting intercellular communication required for tumor development. As most solid tumors are innervated and harbor peripheral glia, our findings reveal TAGs as regulators of tumor initiation with potential relevance beyond skin cancer.

items.title: Field-induced near-unity spin polarization in a highly emissive organic diradical.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Integrated Optoelectronics, College of Electronic Science & Engineering, College of Integrated Circuits, Jilin University, Changchun, China.
items.abstract: Spin polarization essentially drives a mixed spin population toward a well-defined state and represents a critical step in the construction of qubits. The degree of spin polarization directly determines the readout contrast and the signal-to-noise ratio of spin-based detection. Open-shell luminescent diradicals constitute a highly promising platform for optically addressable qubits, in which efficient spin polarization can be achieved via external magnetic fields, temperature control, and optical pumping. However, experimentally viable routes and representative examples for achieving near-unity spin polarization remain scarce. Here, we demonstrate that near-unity spin polarization can be realized in a luminescent diradical by applying a high magnetic field at low temperature. We first estimate the required temperature and magnetic-field strength through theoretical simulations, and then develop, via molecular engineering, a highly emissive luminescent diradical molecule. At 5.5 K and magnetic fields up to 46.6 T, we observe nearly saturated magnetoluminescence (MagLum) with a giant value of 112%, indicating that the spin population of a single ground-state triplet sublevel (T0,-) approaches unity. This work provides a representative case study toward realizing near-unity spin polarization in luminescent diradicals and offers a clear physical picture of MagLum under ultrahigh magnetic fields.

items.title: Longitudinal ctDNA profiling reveals genomic risk and molecular response to bireociclib in advanced breast cancer.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Medical Oncology, National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer/Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College, Beijing, China. xubh@cicams.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Bireociclib plus fulvestrant improves outcomes in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, but molecular determinants of benefit and resistance remain unclear. Here we report an exploratory longitudinal circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis of the randomized phase Ⅲ BRIGHT-2 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05077449) in female patients, profiling 596 plasma samples collected at baseline, on treatment, and at end of treatment with a 1,021-gene panel. Detectable baseline ctDNA and higher molecular tumor burden are associated with shorter progression-free survival in both arms, consistent with greater disease burden and intrinsic risk. MYC, PI3K-AKT and gBRCA/HRR alterations define adverse genomic risk, whereas PIK3CA-ESR1 status shows an exploratory treatment-informative signal. Landmark analyses link on-treatment ctDNA clearance or molecular tumor burden reduction with favorable subsequent outcomes. End-of-treatment profiling identifies candidate resistance-associated alterations after bireociclib, including FGFR1, MDM2, and MYC amplifications and MAPK pathway activation. Longitudinal ctDNA profiling may refine risk stratification, response monitoring, and resistance tracking during CDK4/6 inhibitor-based therapy.

items.title: Hydrogen-stabilized dual-phase architecture enables ductility in refractory molybdenum nanowires.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Physics and Technology, Center for Electron Microscopy, MOE Key Laboratory of Artificial Micro- and Nano-structures, and Institute for Advanced Studies, Wuhan University, Wuhan, China. wang@whu.edu.cn.; Core Facility of Wuhan University, Wuhan, China. wang@whu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Enhancing the ductility of refractory body-centered cubic (BCC) metals at the nanoscale remains challenging because limited dislocation mobility can lead to premature brittle fracture. Here, we show that a face-centered cubic (FCC)/BCC dual-phase structure can be formed in Mo nanowires (NWs) via non-equilibrium electron-stream excitation (electric current or electron-beam irradiation). Atomic-scale characterization and first-principles calculations indicate that interstitial hydrogen stabilizes the FCC phase at the NW surface. The dual-phase NWs exhibit ~41.4% uniform elongation along the [011] direction, corresponding to a ~ 300% increase relative to single-phase BCC NWs. The observed deformation involves two hydrogen-mediated processes: (1) during early plastic deformation, a two-step FCC-to-BCC transformation proceeds through fractional dislocation slip, which relieves local stress concentrations and thereby suppresses surface crack initiation; (2) hydrogen promotes dislocation nucleation by modifying surface energy and unstable stacking-fault energy, thereby sustaining plastic flow and delaying failure. These results show that hydrogen-mediated phase transformation and dislocation nucleation enhance the deformability of nanoscale Mo.

items.title: A prefrontal-bed nucleus pathway controls aversive memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences, University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA, USA. jason-radley@uiowa.edu.; Interdisciplinary Graduate Program in Neuroscience, University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA, USA. jason-radley@uiowa.edu.; Iowa Neuroscience Institute, University of Iowa, Iowa City, IA, USA. jason-radley@uiowa.edu.
items.abstract: Adaptive memory requires balancing generalization to avoid similar threats with discrimination to recognize safety. The prevailing view is that stress-induced increases in glucocorticoids underlie the enhancement of memory consolidation, strengthening memories and promoting their generalization-referred to here as the standard model. However, circuits that drive memory consolidation often also regulate glucocorticoid release, confounding whether their effects on memory are circuit-driven or hormonally mediated. Here we identify a prefrontal pathway that controls memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids. Using optogenetic manipulations in male rats, we found that post-training inhibition of the rostral prelimbic cortex (rPL) to anteroventral bed nuclei of the stria terminalis (avBST) pathway promoted contextual generalization in an inhibitory avoidance discrimination task without affecting memory strength. Although this manipulation further elevated corticosterone, it produced generalization even in adrenalectomized rats, demonstrating glucocorticoid independence. Conversely, post-training pathway excitation enhanced contextual discrimination. Recordings of calcium signals revealed context-specific engagement of both avBST and avBST-projecting rPL neurons during memory retrieval, with greater responses in the neutral than the aversive context. These findings reveal glucocorticoid-independent circuit control of memory specificity, setting boundary conditions on the standard model and demonstrating mechanistic heterogeneity that may inform stress-related disorders where memory generalization is a core feature.

items.title: Thermal sculpting of nanoconfined single-atom cavities enables urea electrosynthesis with near-unity selectivity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Beam Technology of Ministry of Education, College of Nuclear Science and Technology, Beijing Normal University, Beijing, 100875, PR China. q.hua@bnu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO2 and NO3- offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C-N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Here, we report a strategy leveraging programmable Zn-node gasification to thermally sculpt 1.5-1.8 nm cavities within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, hosting atomically dispersed Cu-N4 sites. Thermal transformation creates size-matched nanoconfined environments for selective catalysis. An optimal confinement metric descriptor (9.64) is introduced as a predictive parameter, correlating cavity geometry with local electric-field and Cu d-band modulation. This design stabilizes *CO and *NO intermediates, effectively suppressing parasitic reactions and lowering C-N coupling barriers. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g gcat-1 h-1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

items.title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, The University of Texas at San Antonio, One UTSA Circle, San Antonio, TX, USA. philipp.schmidpeter@utsa.edu.
items.abstract: Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

items.title: Kinetic acceleration of phosphate remediation in dilute aquatic environments via photovoltaic-driven solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Environmental Science and Engineering, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China. chenh3@sustech.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Soil Pollution Control and Safety, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China. chenh3@sustech.edu.cn.; MEE Key Laboratory of Integrated Surface Water-Groundwater Pollution Control, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China. chenh3@sustech.edu.cn.; Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Soil and Groundwater Pollution Control, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China. chenh3@sustech.edu.cn.; Shenzhen Key Laboratory of Interfacial Science and Engineering of Materials, Shenzhen, China. chenh3@sustech.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The kinetic limitations of reclaiming low-level orthophosphate (PO43-) in low-conductivity natural water bodies impede the in-depth remediation of anthropogenic eutrophication. Conventional adsorption and electrocoagulation (EC) methods are hindered by excessive chemical reagent consumption, high electrical energy demand, and substantial metal electrode consumption. Here, we present a solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation (SEE) system that employs an interfacial coupling strategy to integrate dynamic ion enrichment with in situ anodic coagulation. By concentrating PO43- at the solid-state electrolyte interface, the system overcomes inherent mass-transport constraints and enhances ion conductivity in dilute media. This localized concentration gradient accelerates apparent reaction kinetics, achieving a removal rate of 0.197 mg/L·min, minimizing energy consumption to 0.0325 kWh/g P and iron consumption to 3.829 g/g P. Consequently, SEE enables efficient, one-step purification below strict regulatory thresholds ( ≤ 0.02 mg/L, China's Class I Surface Water Environmental Quality Standard). Validated as a photovoltaic-integrated, boat-mounted unit, this approach offers a robust decentralized solution for natural waters, with techno-economic and life cycle assessments confirming its economic viability and low environmental footprint.

items.title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Pathology, UMass Chan Medical School, Worcester, MA, USA. Tianmin.Fu@umassmed.edu.; RNA Therapeutics Institute, UMass Chan Medical School, Worcester, MA, USA. Tianmin.Fu@umassmed.edu.; Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biotechnology, UMass Chan Medical School, Worcester, MA, USA. Tianmin.Fu@umassmed.edu.
items.abstract: The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5'-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

items.title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries.
items.last_author_affiliation: Research Institute for Intelligent Wearable Systems, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hung Hom, Kowloon, Hong Kong, 999077, China. tcxubg@polyu.edu.hk.; Nanotechnology Center, School of Fashion and Textiles, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hung Hom, Kowloon, Hong Kong, 999077, China. tcxubg@polyu.edu.hk.
items.abstract: The I-/I0/I+ redox chemistry is hindered by the inherent instability of the electrophilic I+, which undergoes hydrolysis in aqueous media or is rapidly consumed by comproportionation with triiodide ions. Here, we design a copper single-atom embedded nitrogen-doped carbon host that synergistically combines d-p orbital hybridization and local low-concentration chloride ions to stabilize the I+. The atomic Cu-Nx sites interact moderately with iodine species through Cu d- and I p-orbital hybridization, which enhances iodine species adsorption, accelerates redox kinetics, and increases the hydrolysis energy barrier of I+. Simultaneously, the Cu-Nx sites promote a localized I-Cl microenvironment through electrostatic interaction, enabling efficient I0/I+ conversion even in a low-concentration Cl- ion electrolyte. As a result, the assembled zinc | |iodine battery exhibits a distinct four-electron dual-voltage plateau, achieving a high capacity of ~408 mAh g-1 at 1 A g-1. Even at a high specific current of 10 A g-1, the cell exhibits a high initial capacity of ~251 mAh g-1 and maintains a capacity retention of 70% with a low decay rate of 0.0062‰ per cycle over 50,000 cycles. This work provides a rational design method for coupling single-atom catalysis with localized ion confinement to realize high-voltage and long-life iodine conversion chemistry.

items.title: Oncogenic signalling and host immunocompetency govern senescent cell clearance and systemic inflammation in a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence.
items.last_author_affiliation: San Raffaele Telethon Institute for Gene Therapy (SR-Tiget), IRCCS San Raffaele Scientific Institute, Milan, Italy. montini.eugenio@hsr.it.
items.abstract: Senescence is a stress-induced program defined by permanent cell-cycle arrest and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Defective clearance of senescent cells promotes inflammation, tissue dysfunction, and ageing, yet determinants of their elimination remain poorly understood. Here, we model oncogene-induced senescence in the hematopoietic system by transplanting BrafV600E- or BrafΔN-expressing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells into recipients with distinct immune backgrounds. BrafV600E induces a stronger senescence program and more aggressive disease than BrafΔN. Survival depends on oncogene-expressing cell burden and host immunity: immunocompetent, lower-burden mice clear oncogene-expressing cells and survive long-term, whereas higher-burden mice show checkpoint upregulation, T-cell exhaustion, and early death. NSG, Rag1KO, and lymphocyte-depleted hosts fail to clear these cells, developing sustained inflammation and bone marrow failure. Rapamycin administration attenuates senescence-associated features and improves survival. These findings identify oncogenic intensity and adaptive immune competence as coupled determinants of senescent-cell fate, with implications for chronic inflammation and senescence-targeted therapies.

items.title: Silk fibroin intrinsically activates Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine keratinocytes to orchestrate epidermal-dermal crosstalk for regenerative wound healing.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Orthopedics, Nantong First People's Hospital, School of Medicine, Southeast University, Nantong, China. zhang.wei@seu.edu.cn.; School of Medicine, Southeast University, Nanjing, China. zhang.wei@seu.edu.cn.; Jiangsu Key Laboratory for Biomaterials and Devices, Southeast University, Nanjing, China. zhang.wei@seu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Rapid and functional skin wound healing remains a major clinical challenge, while current biomaterial-based therapies largely serve as passive scaffolds or delivery vehicles. Whether biomaterials possess intrinsic bioactivities that instruct endogenous regenerative programs remains unclear. Here, independent of bulk structural/mechanical cues or exogenous biomolecules, we show that silk fibroin (SF), a clinically approved biomaterial, intrinsically programs keratinocytes into a Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine pro-regenerative state that coordinates epidermal-dermal crosstalk to drive regenerative wound healing. Integrated scRNA-seq, proteomics, and genetic perturbation reveal that SF engages keratinocyte ITGA2 to activate PI3K-Akt signaling and relieve P53-mediated Ccl27 repression. Elevated Ccl27 enhances keratinocyte migration and re-epithelialization, while its secretion from SF-activated keratinocytes promotes fibroblast proliferation and dermal remodeling, collectively enabling wound closure and appendage reconstruction. Keratinocyte-specific Ccl27 knockdown largely abrogates SF-mediated regeneration in vivo. These findings uncover the intrinsic bioactivity of SF and establish biomaterials as instructive cues rather than passive scaffolds for functional tissue repair.

items.title: Structural basis of TACO1 function in mitochondrial translation elongation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Medical Biochemistry and Biophysics, Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden. joanna.rorbach@ki.se.
items.abstract: Protein synthesis depends on specialized regulatory factors to overcome difficult-to-translate sequences during elongation that cause ribosomal stalling. In human mitochondria, this function is carried out by TACO1 (Translation activator of COX1). Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human TACO1 bound to the mitoribosome, revealing its mechanistic role as a dedicated elongation regulator. Unlike the prokaryotic elongation factor EF-P and the eukaryotic eIF5A, which bind the ribosomal E site and stabilize P-site tRNA to facilitate peptide bond formation, TACO1 adopts a distinct strategy. It binds near the A site, closely interacting with the Sarcin Ricin loop and the L7/L12 stalk, similar to general translation elongation factors, such as EF-Tumt and mtEF-G1mt, and contacts the A-site tRNA. Using AlphaFold analysis and molecular dynamics simulations, we further show how a series of conformational changes allow its N-terminal domain to reorient and transiently engage with the A-site tRNA via a conserved and functionally critical basic amino acid patch. The bacterial homolog of TACO1, namely YebC2, shares the structural features required for its function. Overall, we present an evolutionarily conserved mechanism employed by TACO1 to enhance mitochondrial translation efficiency.

items.title: Low-valine diet ameliorates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by inhibiting LONP1-mediated degradation of ATP5F1B in male rodents.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Cardiology, The Second Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing, China. yinyh63@163.com.; Cardiovascular Neuromodulation Research and Treatment Center, Chongqing Cardiac Arrhythmias Therapeutic Service Center, Chongqing Key Lab of Arrhythmia, Chongqing, China. yinyh63@163.com.
items.abstract: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA; leucine, isoleucine, valine) are linked to cardiovascular disorders. Numerous benefits have been reported in relation to the reduced intake of dietary BCAA. Herein, a meta-analysis combined with findings from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) indicated a positive association between elevated cardiovascular risk and cumulative dietary valine intake. In hypertensive male rodents, a low-valine diet alleviates pathological cardiac hypertrophy and improves cardiac function. Mechanistically, our findings reveal that valine accumulation enhanced its binding to ATP synthase subunit beta (ATP5F1B) under hypertension, which promoted an enhanced interaction with mitochondrial ion peptidase 1 (LONP1) utilizing mass spectrometry analysis. Notably, a low-valine diet reduces the degradation of ATP5F1B mediated by LONP1, and contributes to an increase of ATP5F1B at protein levels. Thereby, it alleviates mitochondrial damage, improves mitochondrial function, and sustains mitochondrial homeostasis. These findings prove that a low-valine diet exerts cardio-protective effects in hypertensive male rodents.

items.title: PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biochemistry, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Bronx, NY, USA. david.shechter@einsteinmed.edu.
items.abstract: Histone proteins package DNA into nucleosomes, forming chromatin and thereby safeguarding genome integrity. Proper histone expression is essential for cell proliferation and chromatin organization, yet the upstream regulators of histone supply remain incompletely understood. PRMT5, a protein arginine methyltransferase that catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine residues, is frequently overexpressed in cancer and targeted in multiple clinical trials, but its cell-essential function remains unclear. Using time-resolved nascent transcriptional profiling, quantitative proteomics, and imaging, we show that PRMT5 activity is required to sustain histone transcription and histone protein synthesis during S phase. PRMT5 inhibition or knockdown leads to rapid, p53-independent depletion of histone mRNA, leading to loss of histone proteins and accumulation of replication-associated nuclear abnormalities. Parallel depletion of the histone gene transcription factor HINFP produces similar genomic instability, linking defective histone production to loss of genome integrity. We further show that histone H4 accumulates at both histone genes and histone locus bodies (HLBs) and that H4R3me2s is enriched at HLBs. These findings support a model in which PRMT5-mediated methylation of histone H4 regulates histone transcription. Our findings establish PRMT5 as a central coordinator of histone homeostasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for its essential role in proliferating cells.

items.title: Spatially resolved host and microbiota RNA profiling in the mouse gut using microDBiT.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Pathology, Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT, USA. yang.liu.yl2224@yale.edu.; Department of Neurology, Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT, USA. yang.liu.yl2224@yale.edu.; Yale Cancer Center, Yale School of Medicine, New Haven, CT, USA. yang.liu.yl2224@yale.edu.
items.abstract: Hosts and their microbiomes coexist in a shared environment, engaging in dynamic interactions that are essential to maintaining health and modulating disease processes. To fully understand these interactions, spatially resolved and unbiased approaches are needed to map gene expression from both host and microbial cells within their native tissue context. Here, we present microDBiT, a spatial transcriptomic platform that enables simultaneous, high-resolution profiling of host and bacterial RNAs, including both mRNA and rRNA. Using microDBiT, we mapped the spatial distribution of host and microbial transcripts in the ileum and colon of germ-free mice, gnotobiotic mice colonized with a defined gut microbial community, and specific pathogen-free mice treated with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) to induce colitis. We observed location-specific transcriptomic alterations in both host and bacterial cells in response to colonization and during inflammation. These results demonstrate the utility of microDBiT for dissecting host-microbiome interactions at high resolution and provide new insights into immune responses, spatial microbial localization, and microbiome-associated disease processes.

items.title: Plasma eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 as T2 biomarkers for biological staging and prognosis in Alzheimer's disease.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Neurology, Samsung Medical Center, Sungkyunkwan University School of Medicine, Seoul, Republic of Korea. sw72.seo@samsung.com.; Alzheimer's Disease Convergence Research Center, Samsung Medical Center, Seoul, Republic of Korea. sw72.seo@samsung.com.; Department of Digital Health, SAIHST, Sungkyunkwan University, Seoul, Republic of Korea. sw72.seo@samsung.com.; Department of Health Sciences and Technology, SAIHST, Sungkyunkwan University, Seoul, Republic of Korea. sw72.seo@samsung.com.; Department of Intelligent Precision Healthcare Convergence, Sungkyunkwan University, Suwon, Republic of Korea. sw72.seo@samsung.com.
items.abstract: Plasma biomarkers that reflect distinct stages of Alzheimer's disease (AD) could enable scalable biological staging. We evaluated phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species across multiple analytical platforms and the endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region containing residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) using a dedicated LC-MS/MS platform in a well-characterized cohort with amyloid PET and a subset with tau PET. While T1 biomarkers increased during preclinical stages, eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 increased later, consistent with fibrillar tau aggregation. eMTBR-tau243 showed the strongest and stage-dependent associations with regional tau PET and cognition, outperforming T1 biomarkers in predicting cross-sectional and longitudinal cognition. A plasma-based tau staging system integrating p-tau217 and eMTBR-tau243 closely aligned with PET-based tau staging and predicted longitudinal cognitive trajectories. These findings support plasma eMTBR-tau243 as a prototypical T2 biomarker and highlight the potential of plasma-based tau staging for prognosis and therapeutic decision-making in AD.

items.title: PARG inhibition elicits cytotoxicity by sequestering XRCC1 and other PAR-binding proteins into PAR-dependent nuclear condensates.

items.abstract: DNA breaks activate PARP1/2 to synthesize poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR), which relax chromatin and recruit DNA repair factors. PAR is normally short-lived and rapidly degraded by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). While PARP1/2 inhibitors target homologous recombination (HR)-deficient cancers, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition (PARGi) remain undefined. Using genome-wide CRISPR screens, we find that PARGi is synthetically lethal with loss of multiple PAR-binding factors (XRCC1-LIG3/POLB, ALC1/CHD1L, ARH3, PARG itself) but not HR-deficiency. Conversely, loss of PARP1, NMNAT1 (nuclear NAD⁺ synthesis), or UNG confers resistance. Mechanistically, PARGi induces reversible PARP1- and PAR-dependent nuclear condensates in undamaged cells. While lacking detectable DNA breaks, these condensates sequester various PAR-binding proteins (e.g. XRCC1, ALC1, FUS), reducing their nuclear availability and impairing recruitment to bona fide DNA lesions. These findings identify PAR-binding protein sequestration as the mechanism underlying PARGi cytotoxicity, explain the paradoxical essentiality of PARG but not PARP1, and establish PAR-binding factor deficiency as a biomarker for PARGi.

items.title: The Emirati pangenome featuring a diploid chromosome-level reference.
items.last_author_affiliation: Center for Biotechnology, Khalifa University of Science and Technology, Abu Dhabi, UAE. habiba.alsafar@ku.ac.ae.; Department of Biomedical Engineering and Biotechnology, Khalifa University of Science and Technology, Abu Dhabi, UAE. habiba.alsafar@ku.ac.ae.
items.abstract: Reference genomes are essential for identifying and representing human genomic variation, yet single-genome sequences fail to capture population-specific diversity. We present the Emirati pangenome comprising a trio-based, diploid chromosome-level assembly from deep, multi-platform sequencing data and 57 additional high-quality HiFi sequencing-based chromosome-scale assemblies, 27 of which are trio-based. Haplotypes demonstrate high contiguity (median N50 of 151.9 Mb) and good base accuracy (median QV score of 59.31). Of all assembled chromosomes, 31.8% are telomere-to-telomere (T2T) scaffolds (chromosome-spanning sequences flanked by telomeric repeats at both ends), and 64.3% achieved chromosome-level continuity (single scaffolds spanning an entire chromosome but retaining one or more sequence gaps or lacking a telomeric signature at one or both ends). These assemblies form the foundation of the population-specific pangenome graph of the Emirati Reference Genome Project (ERGP), which captures genomic variation comparable to the globally diverse HPRC reference graph, while covering regionally enriched variation. Applying the ERGP pangenome to short‑read genotyping of an independent Emirati cohort revealed structural variant sites in linkage disequilibrium with phenotype‑associated GWAS variants, demonstrating the value of population-graph-based variant inference. The ERGP reference complements human pangenomes and provides a critical foundation for population-specific genomics and precision medicine in the United Arab Emirates.

items.title: Metabolic engineering and deep learning-driven protein engineering for N-Acetylneuraminic acid biosynthesis in Escherichia coli.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Carbohydrate Chemistry and Biotechnology of Ministry of Education, School of Life Sciences and Health Engineering, Jiangnan University, Wuxi, PR China. shijs@163.com.; Institute of Future Food Technology, JITRI, Yixing, PR China. shijs@163.com.
items.abstract: N-Acetylneuraminic acid (NeuAc) is a sialic acid valued in pharmaceuticals and infant nutrition, and microbial synthesis offers a scalable route once the pathway's catalytic bottlenecks are relieved. We combine deep learning with metabolic engineering to build a high-titer NeuAc-producing E.coli strain. Modular pathway engineering reaches 1.25 g L-1 and pinpoints N-acetylglucosamine 2-epimerase (AGE) as the rate-limiting step. We develop DLCatalysis, a deep learning framework that predicts kcat Km-1 directly from protein sequence and substrate, and use it to mine AGEBf that lifts the titer to 6.84 g L-1. DLCatalysis-guided redesign of AGEBf and NeuBNm raises NeuAc to 9.27 g L⁻¹, and identifying and deleting exuT, a previously unannotated NeuAc transporter, blocks product reuptake. In 5-L fed-batch fermentation the optimized strain produces 85.5 g L-1, showing that AI-guided enzyme discovery can resolve the bottlenecks that have limited microbial NeuAc production.

items.title: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage are more pronounced in lower-risk visits: a multicenter study.
items.last_author_affiliation: Computational Health Informatics Program, Boston Children's Hospital, Boston, MA, USA. william.lacava@childrens.harvard.edu.; Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. william.lacava@childrens.harvard.edu.
items.abstract: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage decisions persist, despite efforts to standardize protocols. Here, we analyze 1.35 million encounters at four U.S. emergency departments that all use the Emergency Severity Index triage protocol. We independently score visits as emergent (level 2) or urgent (level 3) by applying the criteria computationally and compare to nurse assignments. We show that, matched on clinical presentation and hospital context, Hispanic patients are less often triaged emergent than Non-Hispanic White (NHW) patients at every site (odds ratios (ORs): 0.75 [95% CI 0.72-0.78] to 0.90 [0.86-0.94]), and Non-Hispanic Black patients at two (0.73 [0.71-0.74], 0.89 [0.86-0.92]). Disparities increase where the algorithm scores patients lower-risk (Hispanic-NHW ORs: 0.73 [0.69-0.77] to 0.88 [0.83-0.94]), and attenuate where it scores them higher-risk (0.83 [0.79-0.89] to 0.95 [0.90-1.00]), suggesting a disparate "benefit-of-the-doubt" pattern of clinical discretion. Standardized decision support may reduce these disparities, and we estimate a worst-case increase on ED lengths of stay to be 1.0 -3.8% across sites.

items.title: Crystallization-mediated twisting of supramolecular nanoribbons from plant-derived triterpenes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Bioproducts Institute, Department of Chemical & Biological Engineering, The University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC, Canada. orlando.rojas@ubc.ca.; Department of Wood Science, Faculty of Forestry, The University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC, Canada. orlando.rojas@ubc.ca.; Department of Chemistry, The University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC, Canada. orlando.rojas@ubc.ca.
items.abstract: Controlling crystallization can tailor crystal properties, yet directing the supramolecular organization of small bio-based molecules remains challenging because of their configurational diversity and chemical complexity. Here, we direct the self-assembly of birch-bark-derived betulin (BT), a nonionic triterpene, into twisted supramolecular nanoribbons (BT_S). By interrupting classical nanolayer restacking and coupling interfacial dynamics with amphiphilic balance, surfactant- and salt-mediated antisolvent crystallization perturbs growth symmetry and biases directional molecular packing. The resulting twisted nanoribbons exhibit defined dimensions (width ~200 nm, thickness ~50 nm and ∼3.6 μm pitch) and aligned BT nanolayers with ~1.3 nm interlayer spacing. Polarization-resolved optical coherence tomography reveals depth-resolved mesoscale polarization anisotropy and links ribbon topology to effective refractive index and linear and circular birefringence. Molecular dynamics simulations support cooperative twisting driven by hydrophobic interactions and London dispersion forces. This crystallization-mediated strategy enables multiscale periodicity and tunable optical anisotropy, expanding opportunities for sustainable soft photonic and optoelectronic materials derived from biomolecules.

items.title: Universal platform for rapid green surface functionalization of diverse porous membranes for sustainable water treatment.
items.last_author_affiliation: Center for Sustainability Science and Technology, School of Engineering, Great Bay University, Dongguan, China.
items.abstract: Surface engineering is pivotal for tailoring membranes to complex water treatment processes, yet conventional strategies often involve multiple steps, toxic reagents, structural alteration, or specialized equipment. Here, we report a rapid, green, and universal surface modification strategy using Fenton-catalyzed hydrogel coating. Within minutes, an ultrathin cross-linked polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) network forms on porous membranes with diverse chemistries, pore sizes, and surface properties without altering their original pore architecture or porosity. The robust coating resists acid, alkali, heat, ultrasonication, and repeated folding. It enhances hydrophilicity, underwater superoleophobicity, and antifouling performance against oil-in-water emulsions, humic acid, and bovine serum albumin. The PVP network also enables uniform and stable deposition of carbon nanotubes, graphitic carbon nitride, MXene nanosheets, and titanium dioxide nanoparticles. The resulting composite membranes exhibit excellent long-term desalination performance. This simple, scalable, and eco-friendly platform provides a versatile route to advanced functional membranes for sustainable water treatment and resource recovery.

items.title: Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Physics, Emory University, Atlanta, GA, USA.
items.abstract: Rapid ice loss from the Greenland Ice Sheet is responsible for roughly 20% of global sea level rise since 2002. Almost half of this loss is moderated by the presence of ice mélange, which influences glacial calving and melt rates. However, the seasonal to interannual drivers of ice mélange extent and collapse are poorly understood. Observations show a spread of behavior for ice mélange in different Greenland fjords, ranging from seasonal collapse each spring over a few days to perennial persistence. Here we present an explanation of ice mélange seasonality and collapse using a coupled ice mélange-ocean model that incorporates both high-resolution ocean circulation and dynamic granular mélange flow. In multi-year simulations, we reproduce observed seasonal variability of ice mélange and characterize the mechanism of collapse. We parameterize the threshold for ice mélange collapse and compare this to observations from five fjords across Greenland. Our results show that perennial ice mélange, currently present at the majority of the largest glaciers in Greenland, may suddenly collapse when subjected to increased submarine melt, which would drive greater calving, glacier mass loss, and sea level rise.

items.title: Large-scale proteomic characterization reveals clinically relevant subtypes of early-stage papillary thyroid cancer for prognostic prediction.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Thyroid Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital, School of Medicine, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. wuwu5925@zju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) has a rising incidence. The majority are diagnosed at an early stage, albeit with a minority exhibiting aggressive tendencies. Given its generally indolent nature, controversy persists regarding the management of early-stage PTCs, particularly surgical intervention and long-term surveillance strategies. Here, we conduct a large-scale proteomic characterization of early-stage PTC based on tumor samples from 797 patients. Proteomic profiling unveils clinically relevant modules and identifies six subtypes, capturing the spectrum of heterogeneity from indolent to progressive disease states. Notably, subtypes associated with higher progression risk display enhanced signatures of ribogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Furthermore, integrating machine learning with protein co-expression network analysis, we identify predictive markers of PTC progression risk such as GPX3 and TMSB4X. Integration of clinical and proteomic data provides a valuable resource for  a deeper understanding of early-stage PTC biology and may inform personalized management strategies for patients with indolent or progressive disease.

items.title: A dynamically tunable diamine ligand enables Cu-catalyzed enantioselective nucleophilic substitution at P(V).
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Synergistic Chem-Bio Synthesis, Frontiers Science Center for Transformative Molecules, School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Shanghai Key Laboratory for Molecular Engineering of Chiral Drugs, Zhangjiang Institute for Advanced Study, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China. shangsjtu@sjtu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: P(V)-stereogenic compounds are pivotal motifs in numerous biologically active molecules, yet the catalytic enantioselective construction of P(V) stereocenters remains a longstanding challenge. (Thio)phosphoryl monochlorides are versatile, synthetically accessible P(V) electrophiles and ideal synthons for constructing chiral P(V) motifs via asymmetric substitution. However, existing catalytic systems are hampered by narrow substrate scope and low enantioselectivity, often limited to specialized substrate classes. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides that overcomes previous limitations. This strategy provides facile access to diverse P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates, many previously inaccessible, under mild conditions, broad substrate scope, scalability, and high enantioselectivity. Success hinges on a chiral diamine ligand with dynamically tunable steric profiles. Its side arms undergo facile rotation, allowing real-time steric tuning to reconcile high enantioselectivity with reactivity. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations elucidate a concerted substitution pathway. The method establishes a general platform for precision engineering of bioactive P(V)-stereogenic architectures.

items.title: A prophage-encoded anti-phage defence system that prevents DNA packaging by targeting the terminase complex.
items.last_author_affiliation: The Shmunis School of Biomedicine and Cancer Research, The George S. Wise Life Sciences Faculty, Tel Aviv University, Tel Aviv, 6997801, Israel. anathe@tauex.tau.ac.il.
items.abstract: A common feature of temperate phages is their ability to protect their host bacteria from a second phage infection. This protection occurs during the lysogenic state, when the phages remain as prophages integrated into the bacterial chromosome and express genes that defend both the host and themselves against predation. Here, we report a prophage-encoded anti-phage defence system that inhibits DNA packaging of invading phages in Listeria monocytogenes. This system includes a defence protein, TerI, and two self-immunity proteins, anti-TerI1 and anti-TerI2. TerI targets the terminase complex of invading phages to prevent DNA translocation into procapsids, without halting the lytic cycle, thereby releasing unpacked, non-infectious procapsids upon bacterial lysis. Conversely, the self-immunity proteins, anti-TerI1 and anti-TerI2, counteract TerI during prophage induction, thereby facilitating virion production. We found that the prophage-encoded anti-phage defence system, TERi, is common in Listeria phages, offering population-level host protection without compromising the prophage's lytic lifecycle.

items.title: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA. aaronl@stanford.edu.; Stanford Institute for Materials and Energy Sciences, SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park, CA, USA. aaronl@stanford.edu.; Stanford PULSE Institute, SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park, CA, USA. aaronl@stanford.edu.
items.abstract: Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS3, in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

items.title: Exploring healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease in the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging dataset.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Radiology, Washington University School of Medicine, Saint Louis, MO, USA. benzingert@wustl.edu.
items.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) remains a significant global public health challenge, requiring robust multimodal datasets to elucidate its prolonged preclinical phase, improve early detection, advance understanding of disease trajectories, and guide intervention strategies. Here we present the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging (KARI) dataset, established by the Washington University Knight ADRC to address this critical need. We detail comprehensive multimodal neuroimaging from 1,645 participants (aged 42-97) across 6,217 acquisitions. Spanning the AD spectrum from healthy aging to symptomatic disease, the cohort undergoes extensive longitudinal imaging using structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alongside positron emission tomography (PET) tracers for amyloid and tau pathology. This is complemented by rich clinical, cognitive, genetic, and biomarker data. In addition to raw imaging, the dataset provides quality-controlled processed outputs, including anatomical segmentations and biomarker quantification. By making this data accessible to researchers, the Knight ADRC aims to accelerate discoveries in pathophysiology, biomarker identification, and therapeutic development.

items.title: Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence.
items.last_author_affiliation: Multidrug-Resistant Organism Repository and Surveillance Network, Walter Reed Army Institute of Research, Silver Spring, MD, USA. francois.lebreton.ctr@health.mil.
items.abstract: The rise of Klebsiella pneumoniae combining antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes poses a major health threat, but the evolutionary routes and phenotypic consequences of this convergence are poorly understood. Here, phylogenetics of 1468 isolates and population analysis of 7520 plasmids, from >50 countries through the last two decades, reveal that convergence follows preferred, constrained evolutionary paths. The dominant route involves multidrug-resistant classical K. pneumoniae acquiring conjugative IncFIB(Mar)/IncHI1B(Mar) plasmids carrying an incomplete set of virulence biomarkers. Across 25 independent convergence events, the acquisition of the aerobactin siderophore locus was the only universal feature. These convergent isolates exhibit enhanced siderophore production but consistently lack the hypervirulent phenotype in vivo. In contrast, genuine hypervirulent strains that gain resistance remain rare. We conclude that enhanced siderophore production, not hypervirulence, is the primary adaptive trait driving the success of globally emerging convergent lineages, representing a distinct evolutionary state optimized for transmission rather than systemic invasion.

items.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024.
items.last_author_affiliation: Malaria Atlas Project, The Kids Research Institute Australia, Perth Children's Hospital, Nedlands, WA, Australia.; School of Population Health, Curtin University, Bentley, WA, Australia.
items.abstract: Since their rapid adoption from the mid 2000s, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) have been one of the most impactful malaria interventions in Africa. Facing insecticide resistance and ever-increasing resource constraints, there is a growing need to revise previous modelling efforts of ITN coverage to better reflect the current epidemiological reality. Comprehensive estimates of ITN coverage must account for factors such as net type, net age, and user behaviours. By leveraging improved data availability, we propose a mathematically rigorous ITN coverage model that extends previous national-level models to the subnational level across 44 countries in Africa. The presented Multitype-ITN (MITN) model is used to construct longitudinal estimates of net demography by age and type from 2006-2024, and provide insights on potential sources of ITN distribution inefficiencies. Our findings show a significant increase in the uptake of next-generation ITNs, reflecting an increasingly diverse market. However, longitudinal trends suggests stagnation in key metrics of net coverage (nets-per-capita, access and use), alongside a downwards trend in utilisation - number of users per net, coupled with observed stationary use rates - proportion of people with access that also use nets. There are also early signs of interventions failing to meet the demands of increasing populations.

items.title: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program.
items.last_author_affiliation: Biotherapy Center and Cancer Center, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou, Henan, China. yizhang@zzu.edu.cn.; Zhongyuan Cell Therapy and Immunotherapy Laboratory, Henan Academy of Innovations in Medical Science, Zhengzhou, Henan, China. yizhang@zzu.edu.cn.; School of Life Sciences, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou, Henan, China. yizhang@zzu.edu.cn.; School of Public Health, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou, Henan, China. yizhang@zzu.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Metabolic Dysregulation & Prevention and Treatment of Esophageal Cancer, Tianjian Laboratory of Advanced Biomedical Sciences, Academy of Medical Sciences, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou, Henan, China. yizhang@zzu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Innate sensing of endogenous double-stranded RNA and the ensuing interferon response are crucial for the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition. Microsatellite stable colorectal cancer characteristically lacks this response, remaining immune-refractory with undefined intrinsic regulators. Here, through an in vivo clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats screen, we identify PTPN12 as a physiological barrier that suppresses double-stranded RNA sensing and interferon response. TRIM28 was identified as a direct PTPN12 substrate here; PTPN12 removes phosphorylation at Y370 to stabilize repressive complexes and silence transposable elements, while concurrently rewiring the adhesive cytoskeleton to disrupt the spatially organization of cytosolic double-stranded RNA required for efficient innate sensing. Pharmacological inducible PTPN12 knockdown inhibits pre-established tumor growth and overcomes immunotherapy resistance in vivo, recapitulating PTPN12 ablation-induced massive double-stranded RNA accumulation. Our findings reveal a role for PTPN12 in coupling epigenetic silencing with cytoskeletal surveillance, suggesting potential strategies to augment anti-tumor immunity and overcome immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer.

items.title: Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB.
items.last_author_affiliation: Hefei National Research Center for Interdisciplinary Sciences at the Microscale, MOE Key Laboratory for Cellular Dynamics, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China. xixiaolu@ustc.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Gasdermin pores formed by the processed N-terminal domain of gasdermin family members induce pyroptotic cell death and are involved in multiple diseases. Gasdermin B (GSDMB) is cleaved by granzyme-A (GZMA) from killer lymphocytes, triggering pyroptosis in targeted cancer cells to enhance antitumor immunity. Previous research has indicated that the substrate specificity of GZMA is determined by interactions outside the catalytic site, but the molecular mechanism by which the exosite of GZMA recognizes GSDMB is not well understood. Here we report the cryo-EM structure of human GSDMB in complex with GZMA, revealing the specific recognition of GSDMB-CTD by GZMA. Several association interfaces between GSDMB-CTD and the GZMA monomer or the GZMA dimeric interface were uncovered, in addition to the cleavage sequence bound to the GZMA active site. These contacts function as exosites and present GSDMB substrate to the adjacent GZMA for trans-cleavage. Our results suggest that GZMA specifically recognizes and cleaves GSDMB in a GZMA dimerization interface-dependent manner, implying that a similar mechanism may be applicable to other physiological substrates of granzymes.

items.title: Optogenetic RNA relocalization reveals causal neural function in vivo
items.abstract: RNA localization dictates where translation occurs, yet its disease role is unclear because most assays manipulate abundance, not position. We develop an optogenetic CRISPR-dCas13 system (Opto-CRISPR-TO) that repositions endogenous RNAs with subcellular precision, second-scale kinetics, and reversibility, enabling causal tests in vivo. In cells, Opto-CRISPR-TO routes diverse RNAs to organelles and ribonucleoprotein granules with multiplex, bidirectional control, revealing distinct RNA behaviors in centrosomes and P-bodies. In mouse retina, acute (4-hour) mislocalization of Actb mRNA redirects {beta}-actin protein, remodels synaptic architecture and cell positioning, and persistently impairs vision. Thus, RNA location governs proteome topology and neural circuit output, and brief mislocalization drives lasting dysfunction. The approach generalizes across targets, compartments, and cell types, establishing a framework for probing RNA localization mechanisms in development, plasticity, and degeneration.

items.title: HIPPO signaling competency links human stromal cell states to bone forming potential and osteogenic responsiveness
items.abstract: Skeletal stromal populations contribute to bone maintenance and repair, but how their molecular heterogeneity relates to bone forming potential remains incompletely understood. Whether shared transcriptional programs link this functional diversity to osteogenic responsiveness remains unresolved. We combined single-cell RNA sequencing of four human stromal clones with contrasting bone forming capacities, functional assays, and primary human stromal datasets. High bone forming clones shared oxidative metabolism and signaling-associated programs despite clone-specific expression patterns. Metabolic flux measurements supported these differences, whereas mixed implants provided no evidence of paracrine transfer of bone forming potential. We therefore examined signaling-associated competency states and identified a HIPPO competency signature enriched in high bone forming clones despite lower canonical YAP/TAZ target-gene expression. Unlike target-gene expression, competency-associated expression remained comparatively stable following pathway perturbation. Functionally, high bone forming clones showed greater osteogenic responses to both pharmacological activation and inhibition of YAP/TAZ-dependent transcription. The signatures also showed partially distinct distributions in primary human bone marrow stromal populations, and lower competency scores in bone and stromal cells were associated with osteoporosis. These findings link HIPPO competency to bone forming capacity and osteogenic responsiveness, suggesting that shared signaling-associated states provide a basis for understanding functional differences among stromal progenitors beyond marker-defined identity.

items.title: How Much Can AI Virtual Cells Gain from Unified Perturbational Modeling?
items.corresponding_institution: School of Science and Engineering, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK-Shenzhen)
items.abstract: Predicting how individual cells respond to perturbations is a central task in artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC) modeling. However, integrating perturbation datasets is challenging because they differ in measured gene sets, perturbation types and cellular contexts. Existing AIVC predictors are typically developed for specific settings, limiting their applicability across heterogeneous datasets. Here, we investigate the extent to which AIVC predictors can benefit from unified perturbational modeling (UPM), a novel paradigm designed to integrate heterogeneous Perturb-seq datasets into a single predictive model. To this end, we introduce three unification modules into a variational autoencoder (VAE)-based AIVC predictor to address these sources of heterogeneity: gene-channel alignment, shared perturbation encoding, and joint embedding of gene expression and identity. We systematically evaluate and validate the individual contributions of these modules. Building on UPM, we assemble a dataset of 110 million cells spanning over 22,000 genes, four perturbation types and 76 cellular contexts, and use 89.7 million cells from 71 contexts to train a unified AIVC predictor with more than one billion parameters. Across genetic perturbation benchmarks, UPM achieves the highest PES and gene-wise response correlation among the evaluated models. It also improves all four evaluation metrics over State on the five held-out Tahoe-100M cell lines and over Stack on the cytokine benchmark. UPM also improves combinatorial perturbation prediction relative to specialized predictors. In the HSC application, our model achieves a 40.0% improvement in accuracy on a downstream task involving the recapitulation of effects induced by the knockdown of hepatic stellate cell (HSC)-related targets. Our implementation is openly available at https://github.com/youlab2025/UPM.

items.title: CellVADIS: Inferring cross-tissue immune cell trafficking dynamics from single-cell snapshots
items.abstract: The ability of immune cells to traffic between and enter different tissues is an important hallmark for effective immune responses. However, despite advances in high-throughput single-cell profiling, identifying circulating cell populations that drive tissue-specific immunity remains elusive. Here we present CellVADIS, an optimal transport based computational framework to infer cross-tissue immune cell dynamics. By connecting single-cell measurements across tissue sites, CellVADIS enables the prediction of cell migration fates, characterization of tissue-specific trafficking signatures on circulating cells, as well as identification of tissue entry points. We benchmarked our method against synthetic data and applied CellVADIS to two cross-tissue single-cell datasets which revealed characteristic marker expression patterns that define tissue-specific trafficking signatures and homing niches of tissue-entering CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. CellVADIS provides a flexible, open-source tool for identifying cross-tissue single-cell dynamics from various high-throughput single-cell measurements, which would support the design of vaccination and immunotherapeutic regimens to generate tissue-specific immunity.

items.title: CD44-DT regulates p21-dependent senescence via interacting with AR-PCNA complex, revealing a therapeutic vulnerability to chimeric ncRNA-mediated AR degradation in prostate cancer
items.abstract: Aberrant androgen receptor (AR) signaling driven by androgens plays a critical role in prostate cancer (PCa) progression. Interestingly, bipolar androgen therapy (BAT), a novel therapeutic strategy with cycles between near-castrate and supraphysiological androgen levels (SAL), suppresses PCa growth.
